title: Progressive shard defragmentation and NCCL pacing proposal
content:
Status: draft

Purpose
- Capture design for a low-disruption, online mechanism to reduce fragmentation across multi-GPU shard placements and to smooth NCCL collective bursts ("NCCL pacing"). Goal: lower tail latency and variance during dynamic workload shifts without heavy rendezvous/eviction.

Motivation / problem statement
- Shard fragmentation accumulates when workloads change (new model variants, transient requests, cold starts). Small, straggling shards increase cross-GPU traffic and cause frequent small NCCL collectives with poor bandwidth utilization.
- Current approach (full reshuffle or immediate eviction) is either expensive or causes request-level disruption. We need progressive background rebalancing with bandwidth-aware collectives.

High-level design
1) Progressive Shard Defragmenter (PSD): background actor that identifies micro-imbalances and coalesces adjacent shard ranges into fewer destinations over time. Works with shard metadata (epoch, owner, live-FANOUT) and uses per-GPU slack windows to apply moves. Moves are incremental: move small KV ranges, update routing metadata atomically, and allow in-flight inference to drain with versioned keys.

2) NCCL Pacing Layer: thin shim around collective launch (ring/allreduce/allgather) that inserts lightweight pacing decisions based on current interconnect utilization and QoS budget. It can: stagger launches across groups, insert micro-delays, or coalesce small collects into batched multi-collectives when safe. Has heuristics: prefer pacing when avg collective size < X tokens or when cross-host NIC utilization > 60%.

3) Kernel Splitter / Partial-layer assignment: allow expensive layers to be logically split across GPUs (sub-layer tiling) so that PSD can prefer coalescing whole tiles instead of scattering activations across many devices. The runtime exposes an API for kernel authors to indicate split points and tolerated KV fragment sizes.

Key invariants and safety
- Consistency: router epoch for keys increments atomically so replicas can serve old epoch until migration completes. Small window of dual-serving allowed (read-only) with strict write-to-master rules.
- Latency SLOs: PSD yields when 99.9th percentile latency approaches configured threshold for the pool. Pacing layer can preempt rebalancing to prioritize requests.

Instrumentation and metrics
- New metrics: shard_fragmentation_ratio (per pool), average_collective_bytes, paced_collective_fraction, rebalancer_moves/sec, dual-serving_percentage, move_latency_distribution.
- Dashboards: per-pool timeline showing fragmentation, pacing decisions, and tail latency correlation.

Rollout and experiments
Phase 0: Simulation using historical traces to tune thresholds and batch sizes.
Phase 1: Canary on test fleets (non-production) with metrics-only mode (no actual moves).
Phase 2: Passive rebalancer (precompute migrations, but requires manual approval).
Phase 3: Active progressive rebalancer with NCCL pacing enabled on low-risk pools.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- How aggressively can we dual-serve before risking consistency surprises for stateful plugins?
- What is the optimal batching window for coalescing small collectives without adding latency?
- Interaction with autoscaling: rebalancer should consider imminent node termination/placement decisions to avoid wasted moves.

Implementation notes / TODOs
- API: Extend shard metadata proto with epoch, preferred_tiles, and move_priority.
- Rebalancer: implement in runtime as a background gRPC worker with leader election via existing placement service.
- NCCL shim: prototype at user-space level (LD_PRELOAD style) for rapid iteration before kernel integration; measure jitter introduced by pacing.
- Tests: unit tests for routing epoch handoff; integration test that injects simulated fragmentation and verifies tail-latency improvement.

References / related work
- See JIRA ticket JIRA-ENG-1423 for measurement notebook.
- Related kernel fusion notes: /serving-runtime/opportunistic-replication-and-kernel-fusion-sketch (informational).

Next steps
- Run trace simulation (Mateo) by 2026-02-05.
- Prototype NCCL pacing shim (Rina) and measure on 4xA100 rig.
- Wire up migration metadata and small-scale canary (Jonas).

Notes to self
- Keep early rollout conservative; prioritize reduced variance over absolute median gains.
- Expect multiple tuning cycles for pacing thresholds across cloud vs on-prem.
